item.title: MJR Morning Brief — November 20, 2026
item.description:
From Media Jobs Report, this is the MJR Morning Brief.
The U.S. Department of Labor has announced new rules for determining whether workers are employees or independent contractors, replacing standards adopted in 2024. The changes could affect media companies that hire freelance reporters, producers, on-air talent and other contract professionals. The new guidelines focus on how much control a company has over a worker and whether that individual operates an independent business. Read more about the changes and what they could mean for media employers at Media Jobs Report dot com.
Turning to television,
The FCC has set January 11, 2027, as the effective date for eliminating the national television ownership cap. The rule previously limited how much of the nation's television audience a single broadcaster could reach through station ownership. Its repeal could open the door for major television groups to acquire additional stations.
In radio news,
Glenn Beck is inviting listeners home for Christmas. The Premiere Networks host will be joined by his daughter, recording artist Cheyenne Grace, family and friends for the three-hour *It’s Christmas Again* holiday special. The program features Christmas memories, family traditions, faith, laughter and music from Grace’s new Christmas album. Stations can begin airing the special December 21 and run it multiple times during Christmas week.
Turning to podcasts,
Triton Digital has released its October U.S. Podcast Ranker, and *Pod Save America* takes the top spot! Rounding out the top five podcasts are *Stuff You Should Know* at number two, *My Favorite Murder* at number three, *The Dan Bongino Show* at number four, and *The Bulwark Daily* at number five. On the network side, iHeart Audience Network leads with more than 68 million average weekly downloads, followed by Audioboom at number two, Cumulus Podcast Network at number three, BBC at number four, and American Public Media Group at number five.
On the business side of media,
Three major television broadcasters are heading to upcoming investor conferences. Nexstar Media Group, Gray Media and Sinclair have scheduled appearances at financial events through December, with Gray also planning an appearance in March. All three companies will participate in the BofA leveraged finance conference, while Nexstar and Sinclair will also appear at the Wells Fargo TMT Summit. Several presentations will be available by webcast. Read more media financial news at Media Jobs Report dot com.
Turning to television,
Telemundo 49 Tampa has promoted Gilberto Dorrego to Anchor of its 6 p.m. newscast. Beginning November 23, Dorrego will join Andrea González at the anchor desk for *Noticiero Telemundo 49*. He'll also continue leading the station's consumer investigative unit, *Telemundo 49 Responde*. Dorrego joined the station in 2025 and previously worked at Telemundo stations in Arizona, San Diego and Dallas-Fort Worth.
And finally,
Key Networks has renewed its longtime partnership with Virtual Jock, continuing to bring major-market radio talent and programming services to stations across the country. Now entering their seventh year together, the partnership gives stations access to more than 85 experienced on-air personalities, along with remote programming, localized content, traffic, weather, station imaging and commercial production. Services are available to stations of all sizes through cash or barter agreements.
Find more media news, jobs, industry resources and free tools at MediaJobsReport.com.
